E400.description: The request is malformed: a missing or invalid parameter, or an unsupported format.

E404.description: No such project, item, sprint or document.

E409.description: The board was written by a newer kanbanr than this daemon; upgrade it.

E500.description: The board could not be read.

Action.description: Something that happens when an item enters a status.

oneOf.description: `kanbanr start` creates the item's branch here (where the project is a git repository).

actor.description: Who made the change (the commit identity name).

item.description:
The work item (feature code) this change touched, when applicable — enables per-item and
per-kind activity streams. Serialized as `item`.

message.description: A short human description of the change.

Adr.description: An architecture decision record: front-matter plus the prose it belongs to.

decided.description: When the decider accepted or rejected it (FEAT-153). `date` is when it was proposed.

driven_by.description: The requirements that forced it, usually quality ones: `FEAT-046/R-2`.

missing.description:
The scaffolded sections it leaves unanswered, as `list` reports them — so the Review page
can say why Accept is refused without a second copy of the rule (FEAT-153). Never stored.

path.description: Where it lives in the doc tree.

quality.description: ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics at stake — the shared vocabulary with NFRs.

reason.description: Why it was rejected: a rejected decision is still a record, and its reason is the record.

superseded_by.description: Written by `adr supersede`, never by hand.

trade_offs.description: The machine-readable summary of the Consequences prose.

ApprovalEvent.description:
Agreement to a definition, pinned to its content (FEAT-048).

`rev` is a hash of the definition as approved. If the definition changes afterwards the hash no
longer matches and the approval has **lapsed** — so scope cannot drift silently past a "yes",
which is exactly how work gets built and then rejected.
One agreement, or one withdrawal of it (FEAT-069). Append-only: an approval that was given and
later taken back is more informative than no record at all, and the charter constraint says raw
data is never discarded.

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn. An agreement needs no reason; taking one back does.

rev.description: The definition content this verdict was about.

status.description:
The status the item was in when the verdict was given (FEAT-114), so a definition that grows
stage by stage leaves a readable trail: approved at Vision, again at System Design.

verdict.description:
`approved` | `ratified` | `withdrawn`.

`ratified` is agreement given **after** the work was built, under a recorded
`--unapproved` start (FEAT-080). It is a separate verdict from `approved` because the
whole point of the gate is to distinguish "we agreed, then built" from "we built, then
agreed" — and with one verdict the record could not tell them apart. Twenty-nine items on
this board were reconciled that way before the distinction existed.

ApprovalKind.description: The question a review entry asks.

oneOf.description: Finished under a recorded bypass and never agreed to (FEAT-109): ratify it.
Agreed; the stage it reaches next waits on a sign-off (FEAT-117).
Agreed, and nothing to sign: which release it ships in (FEAT-185).
Defined, never approved.
Approved, then the definition changed.

BoardCard.description: A single feature as it appears on the cross-project board.

status.description: The feature's native (per-project) status — kept for display, since lanes are normalized.

BoardLane.description: One normalized lane plus its cards (across all projects).

BoardReport.description:
The cross-project board: every feature in the portfolio grouped into the normalized lanes
{not-started, in-progress, done}. Robust to differing per-project workflows because grouping is
derived from each project's own config (Completed-name / no-op) + task activity, not a shared
status vocabulary.

BurndownDay.description: One day of a burndown: what was still to do at the end of it.

Cadence.description: A project's rhythm (FEAT-121): whether it has sprints and releases, and their defaults.

git_model.description:
Branching follows the derived git model (FEAT-189): where `start` branches, sprint
branches, and lines of integration taking merges only. Off by default, so no board changes.

integration_branch.description: The branch a release branch is made from. Unset: the code repository's default branch.

main_branch.description: The branch production is fast-forwarded onto. Unset: the code repository's default branch.

release.description: How often a release is cut: `per_sprint`, `every_n` sprints, or `on_demand`.

release_stages.description:
The environments a release moves through, in order (FEAT-183). The last one is the cut.
Empty means [`DEFAULT_RELEASE_STAGES`]; read it through [`Cadence::stages`].

sprint_length_days.description: The length `sprint add` uses when none is given.

CardReadiness.description: One card's readiness: its gaps, and its next stages.

Charter.description: The reasoning root of a project.

adopted_at.description:
When the charter was first written. Gap reporting ignores items created before this, so
adopting the method never floods the report with pre-existing work.

goals.description: Outcomes this project commits to. Work items link these by id.

non_goals.description: What this project deliberately will not do — often the most useful section.

purpose.description: Why the project exists — the problem or opportunity.

vision.description: Optional one-line statement of the desired end state.

Check.description:
A condition an item can be checked against. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: a workflow can
only require what kanbanr knows how to evaluate from the board.

oneOf.description: The item has a definition at all.
A one-sentence statement: what, for whom, why.
All six Zachman dimensions answered.
Linked to at least one charter goal.
Every linked goal exists in the charter (needs the charter; an error, not a warning).
Agreement is current: approved, or ratified after the fact.
A recorded bypass has been answered (approved or ratified).
At least one requirement.
Every requirement is in EARS form.
Every requirement names a test.
Every requirement has a green test.
Quality requirements carry a valid ISO 25010 tag and a scenario whose measure names its test.
INVEST "Small": not estimated above three days.

Estimated in the project's unit — story points or days (FEAT-121). A Definition of Ready
usually asks for it.
Planned into the project's active sprint (FEAT-119).
Planned into a release (FEAT-120).

A named sign-off is recorded against the current definition. Asked for through a gate's
`signoffs: [name]`, never listed on its own — it needs the name.

The spec has each named section, with content (FEAT-179). A design stage asks for the
design itself, not a promise of one: `{spec_sections: [Design]}`.

Every doc the item declares in `affects_docs` has changed since it entered its current
stage (FEAT-180) — the design was folded into the docs it said it would change.

Condition.description:
One condition a gate can name: a check, or the Zachman check narrowed to some columns
(`{zachman: [what, who, why]}`), which is how a process asks for the six dimensions a stage at a
time rather than all at once.

Counts.description:
Feature-completion counts + a derived percentage. Completion is **status-aware**: a feature in a
terminal status (Completed / no-op) counts as fully done even if it tracks no tasks (many
features are completed by a status move, not by checking off tasks); a non-terminal feature with
tasks gets partial credit (`done/total`); otherwise it's 0. `percent` is the mean per-feature
completion across the group (rounded), or `0` when there are no features. `tasks_*` are retained
for display (how many checklist items exist/are done) but no longer drive the percentage.

Defect.description:
What a defect cost and where it came from (FEAT-053).

`escaped` is the field that earns its keep: a defect found after the work was called done is a
different animal from one caught during it, and the ratio between them is the one quality
number a board can honestly produce.

escaped.description: Found after the work was called done.

fixed_by.description: The commit or test that proves it is fixed.

found_in.description: Where it was found: a status, an environment, or "production".

introduced_by.description:
The item or commit that introduced it. A defect caused by a fix points at that fix, which
is how fix-induced chains become visible.

severity.description: Free text, like `kind` and `priority`: low | medium | high | critical.

Disposition.description:
A project-independent lane a feature falls into, since statuses are per-project (no shared
vocabulary). Computed from the project config + the feature's task activity.

oneOf.description: Terminal: a "Completed"-named status OR a no-op disposition.
Active and has some task activity (at least one task, not all done).
Active but no task activity yet.

path.description: Path relative to the project docs root (forward-slashed), e.g. `design/customer/overview.md`.

title.description: Display title (derived from the file name).

DocFolder.description: A documentation folder node (renders as a tile with sub-folders + documents as links).

path.description: Path relative to the docs root (empty string for the root), forward-slashed.

Drift.description: How a project's workflow stands against the saved process it was applied from (FEAT-170).

edited.description: The project's workflow no longer matches what was applied: someone edited it since.

gone.description: The saved process is no longer in its library.

newer.description: The saved process has changed since: its current version, when it has one.

Enforce.description: Whether a failed gate stops the move or only reports.

EstimateUnit.description: The unit a project estimates in.

FeatureDefinition.description:
Why a work item exists, what must be true, and how that is verified (FEAT-047).

The prose case *for* the work stays in the item's specification markdown — this block holds the
short, checkable parts: one-line answers, ids that link to the charter, and requirements each
carrying the tests that verify them. Keeping it one-line-per-field is deliberate: a structured
copy of the spec would rot into a second, disagreeing version of the same argument.

affects_docs.description:
Board docs this item changes (FEAT-180), e.g. "architecture/data.md". Declared at the design
stage; `docs_updated` checks each was changed before the item moves on. Declared last, so a
board where it is the only key an older binary does not know reads back byte for byte.

approval.description: Who agreed to this definition, when, and what exactly they agreed to (FEAT-048).

approvals.description:
Every agreement and withdrawal, oldest first (FEAT-069). `approval` is the current one, or
absent when the last verdict was a withdrawal.

design_doc.description: Optional pointer into the board's doc tree (a design note), rather than an inline diagram.

exempt.description:
A recorded reason this item is exempt from gap reporting. An escape hatch that is visible
beats one that is habitual (`--no-verify` teaches itself).

goals.description: Charter goal ids this item serves — the link that makes "why" checkable rather than prose.

signoffs.description:
Named agreements a stage can require (FEAT-114): "design review held", "release approved".
Appended, never overwritten — each pinned to the definition it covered.

started_unapproved.description:
A recorded reason work started without approval. An escape hatch that leaves a trace beats
one that is silent — an unrecorded bypass just teaches itself.

statement.description: One sentence: what, for whom, and why.

zachman.description: The six completeness dimensions, one line each.

FeatureExport.description:
An item as `GET /projects/{p}/features/{code}/export?format=json` gives it: the item, and its
milestone resolved.

assignee.description: Optional assignee (the person/agent owning this feature); free text.

defect.description: For a defect: what it cost and where it came from (FEAT-053).

definition.description: Why this item exists, what must be true, and how it is verified (FEAT-047).

depends_on.description: Other feature codes this one is blocked by (a cross-feature DAG; cycles are rejected).

due.description: Optional due date (e.g. an ISO date).

estimate_days.description:
Optional estimated effort, in days (used as the task duration for scheduling/Gantt;
defaults to 1 day when absent). Kept as a float so half-days etc. are expressible.

history.description:
Every status change, appended (FEAT-053). Cycle time, time-in-status, WIP aging and rework
are all derived from this; without it the board records where work IS but never how it got
there.

issue.description: The external issue this feature is mirrored to, if any (FEAT-043).

kind.description: Work kind (feature / chore / bug / refactor / docs / recurring …); free text.

milestone.description: The milestone this feature belongs to (required).

points.description:
Optional estimate in story points (FEAT-121). Which of the two a project plans in is its
`estimate_unit`; absent stays absent on disk.

release.description: The release this item is planned into (FEAT-120), for projects that use releases.

source.description: Where this feature was imported from, if it was (FEAT-042).

split_from.description:
The item this was sliced out of (FEAT-054). A wave grows for three reasons — a defect, a
split, or newly discovered work — and only this one leaves no other trace, so a retro that
tried to infer it would be guessing.

sprint.description: The sprint this item is planned into (FEAT-119), for projects that use sprints.

start.description: Optional planned start date (an ISO date, e.g. "2026-07-01"). Used by scheduling/Gantt.

todo_lists.description: Persistent todo-lists (newest-first ordering is applied by callers when displaying).

FeatureItem.description: A feature item: the unit Claude develops. Holds the spec and its todo list.

assignee.description: Optional assignee (the person/agent owning this feature); free text.

defect.description: For a defect: what it cost and where it came from (FEAT-053).

definition.description: Why this item exists, what must be true, and how it is verified (FEAT-047).

depends_on.description: Other feature codes this one is blocked by (a cross-feature DAG; cycles are rejected).

due.description: Optional due date (e.g. an ISO date).

estimate_days.description:
Optional estimated effort, in days (used as the task duration for scheduling/Gantt;
defaults to 1 day when absent). Kept as a float so half-days etc. are expressible.

history.description:
Every status change, appended (FEAT-053). Cycle time, time-in-status, WIP aging and rework
are all derived from this; without it the board records where work IS but never how it got
there.

issue.description: The external issue this feature is mirrored to, if any (FEAT-043).

kind.description: Work kind (feature / chore / bug / refactor / docs / recurring …); free text.

milestone.description: The milestone this feature belongs to (required).

points.description:
Optional estimate in story points (FEAT-121). Which of the two a project plans in is its
`estimate_unit`; absent stays absent on disk.

release.description: The release this item is planned into (FEAT-120), for projects that use releases.

source.description: Where this feature was imported from, if it was (FEAT-042).

split_from.description:
The item this was sliced out of (FEAT-054). A wave grows for three reasons — a defect, a
split, or newly discovered work — and only this one leaves no other trace, so a retro that
tried to infer it would be guessing.

sprint.description: The sprint this item is planned into (FEAT-119), for projects that use sprints.

start.description: Optional planned start date (an ISO date, e.g. "2026-07-01"). Used by scheduling/Gantt.

todo_lists.description: Persistent todo-lists (newest-first ordering is applied by callers when displaying).

Gap.description: One thing an item is missing.

label.description: Short form, for a one-line list (`[MISSING: What]`, `no goal link`).

message.description: What is missing and what to do about it.

requirement.description: The requirement the gap is about, for per-requirement checks.

Gate.description: The entry criteria of one status. Every field is optional; an empty gate asks nothing.

done.description:
Reaching this stage finishes an item for the cadence views — the sprint burndown, its done
total, what a closing sprint carries over (FEAT-137). Scrum's Definition of Done is the Done
column, not the release that ships it, and a burndown that waited for the release dropped in
one step on release day.

enforce.description: `block` (the default) refuses the move; `warn` allows it and reports what `requires` lacks.

kinds.description:
When set, the gate applies only to items of these kinds (an item with no kind is a
`feature`).

purpose.description: What this stage is for, in a sentence — shown to Claude and in the monitor.

requires.description: Conditions that must hold to enter.

roles.description:
The stage roles this status holds (FEAT-188): `design`, `build`, `integrate`, `release`. The
method and git automation find their stage by role, so they behave the same in every
process. Kept as names, so an unknown one is a reported problem, not a parse failure.

signoffs.description: Named sign-offs that must be recorded against the current definition (FEAT-114).

Goal.description: An outcome the project commits to, not an output it produces.

id.description: `G-1`, `G-2`, … Assigned on save when left blank.

measure.description: How we would know it happened.

IssueLink.description: A link from a feature to the external issue it is mirrored to (FEAT-043).

synced_hash.description: Hash of the issue content kanbanr last pushed; `None` until the first push.

confidence.description: How much it was believed at `last_affirmed`. What is *reported* decays from here.

evidence.description: What actually happened — the part that makes it a lesson rather than an opinion.

history.description: Every affirmation and contradiction, so the number can be explained rather than trusted.

lesson.description: The lesson itself, in one sentence a person can act on.

tags.description: Labels it applies to, so it can be offered to the right work.

oneOf.description: Something that worked and is worth repeating.
Something that cost us, and how to avoid it.
A choice made once that later work should not relitigate.
Recorded, not yet confirmed by anything else.
Confirmed at least once.
Fell below the threshold, or was contradicted. Kept, not surfaced.
A broken reference, not a judgement: someone can fix it by editing a name.

Library.description: Where a saved process lives (FEAT-169), in the order a name is looked up.

oneOf.description: `<board>/processes/`: shared with everyone who has the board, through its remote.
`~/.kanbanr/processes/`: this user's, on any board.
Carried by the binary.

Meta.description: What this daemon can do: `GET /api/meta`. The monitor asks before offering an action.

identity.description:
Who an approval recorded here would be attributed to (FEAT-077): the board's git
identity. Null when there is none, and the monitor then refuses to offer the action.

schema_version.description: The board schema this build understands (FEAT-072).

writes.description: Whether the write routes are mounted (`serve --allow-writes`, FEAT-034).

MethodChoice.description: What a project chose. Absent on disk means never chosen: everything on.

chosen_at.description: When the project last chose (RFC 3339); empty when it never has.

off.description: The parts switched off, sorted and unique.

Milestone.description: A milestone groups feature items and may depend on other milestones (the DAG).

NextGate.description: What moving an item on to one next status would ask, and what it still lacks (FEAT-117).

requires_gaps.description:
What `requires` alone still lacks, without the sign-offs (FEAT-182): a sign-off is offered
only once this is empty, so nobody signs off work that has not happened yet.

signoffs_needed.description: The sign-offs this gate still needs, by name, so a surface can offer to record them.

NextStage.description: A next stage on a card: its status, and how many things it still lacks.

oneOf.description: The spec has a Design section before build.
A person signs off the design before build.
The docs the item names were updated before it integrates.
A person signs off that the design was folded into the docs.
Doctor reports references to things the board does not have.

PortfolioView.description:
The portfolio index as a serializable view: the workspace metadata + programs, with the implicit
default program materialized when none are declared (so callers always see a consistent shape).

ProcessSource.description: Which saved process a project's workflow came from, and which version of it (FEAT-169).

rev.description: The content rev of what was applied ([`WorkflowFile::content_rev`]).

version.description: The process's version when it was applied; 0 for a built-in one.

ProcessStatus.description: How a project stands against its saved process (FEAT-170): `GET /projects/{p}/process`.

drift.description:
How it has moved apart from that process; null when there is nothing to compare, or the
process is a personal one, which only the user's own kanbanr can see.

messages.description: [`Drift::messages`]: one sentence per thing to report.

source.description: The process the project's workflow was applied from; null when none was.

implicit.description: True when this is the synthesized implicit default program (no workspace.yaml programs).

branch_pattern.description:
How `kanbanr start` names a branch (FEAT-056): `{code}` and `{slug}`. Absent means the
default, and absent stays absent on disk so an existing config is not rewritten.

cadence.description:
Whether this project works in sprints and releases at all (FEAT-121). Off unless switched
on: many projects follow a different workflow, and data nobody asked for is clutter.

default_state.description: The status assigned to a newly-created feature item. Must be one of `statuses`.

displayed_states.description: Ordered subset of `statuses` shown on the dashboard.

estimate_unit.description: What this project estimates in (FEAT-121): days, or story points.

gates.description:
Entry criteria per status (FEAT-113): what an item must show before it may move into that
status, and what happens when it does. Absent means today's rules, synthesised by
[`ProjectConfig::effective_gates`]; absent stays absent on disk.

method.description:
Which parts of the method this project turned off, and when it chose (FEAT-193). Absent:
never chosen, everything on.

no_op_states.description:
Subset of `statuses` that are functionally inert dispositions (e.g. "No Action",
"Not Applicable", "Out-of-Scope"). No-op states are always non-displayed, and a feature
in a no-op state does not auto-advance to "Completed" when its tasks finish.

process.description:
The saved process this workflow was applied from, if it was (FEAT-169): what drift is
measured against. An older kanbanr keeps it through `extra`, so it needs no schema bump.

schema_version.description:
On-disk schema version. Absent in legacy configs (defaults to 0); forward-stamped to
`CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` whenever the config is written.

terminal_states.description:
Subset of `statuses` that are explicit terminal (end) states of the workflow — a feature
here is considered "done". Absent in legacy configs (defaults to empty), in which case
`graph::is_terminal_status` falls back to its built-in heuristic (Completed / no-op).

transitions.description: Map of from-status -> list of allowed to-statuses.

ProjectReadiness.description: The board's live cards, keyed by item code, in board order.

ProjectSummary.description: One project on the board, as the home page lists it: `GET /projects`.

counts.description: Items per status, for every status.

displayed_states.description: The statuses shown as board columns.

name.description: The project's name; its id when it has none.

other_states.description: The statuses that are not columns.

QualityScenario.description:
Stimulus / environment / response / measure — what turns "it should be fast" into something
checkable. The `measure` names the test or benchmark that checks it; a number with nothing
behind it is reported as an unsupported claim.

ReadinessView.description:
What one item is missing, and what its next stage asks (FEAT-112, FEAT-117):
`GET /projects/{p}/features/{code}/readiness`.

next.description: What each next stage asks, and what it still lacks.

rev.description:
The definition's revision: a verdict given with `rev` is refused if it moved on
(FEAT-159). Null when the item has no definition.

ReleaseCarry.description: A planned item that did not ship, and where it went.

to.description: The release it moved to, or `unplanned`.

ReleaseReport.description:
A release with what it holds and how much of that is finished, as the monitor shows it
(FEAT-138). Derived, never stored.

branch.description: The code branch, set when promoted to the first stage (`release/<V>`).

finished.description:
How many of `items` are finished, by the same rule as the sprint's: an end status, or a stage
marked `done` (FEAT-137). The page used to keep its own copy of the rule, counting only the
end status — a Done item in a planned scrum release read as unfinished.

included.description: For a patch: what its parent shipped, which the patch keeps (FEAT-184).

items.description: Planned into it, or shipped in it.

notes_doc.description: The board doc holding its release notes.

parent.description: The cut release this patches (FEAT-184); empty for an ordinary release.

stage.description:
Where the release is now, from `cadence.release_stages` (FEAT-183). Empty until first
promoted: a release added before stages existed reads as "not yet a candidate".

Requirement.description: One requirement: a single behaviour, stated so it can be tested.

scenario.description: The quality attribute scenario behind an NFR.

tests.description: How this requirement is verified. A requirement with no test is not ready.

text.description:
The requirement itself, ideally in EARS form. Stored verbatim: the EARS pattern is derived
when rendering or checking, never persisted, so stored text cannot disagree with the
classifier.

violates.description:
For a defect: the requirement it violates (`FEAT-046/R-2`), or blank when the defect
reveals that no requirement covered the case — which is itself the finding.

RequirementKind.description: Functional behaviour, or a quality the system must exhibit.

in_progress.description: What the ordering keys on, and useful to a client besides.

release_choices.description:
The planned releases it could ship in, in file order (FEAT-185). Present whenever the
release question is due, so a surface asking another question first can ask this one too.
Empty: only a new release to choose.

rev.description: What a verdict given from this brief is pinned to (FEAT-159).

signoffs_needed.description: The sign-offs the next stage still needs, by name; empty unless `approval` is `signoff`.

RollupReport.description: The full rollup tree: milestone% → project% → program% → portfolio%.

Signoff.description:
A named agreement, recorded by a person against the definition as it stood (FEAT-114).

Like an approval it carries the definition's `rev`, so changing the definition afterwards lapses
it: a design review of a different design is not a review of this one.

doc.description: A board doc holding the record — minutes, a checklist.

id.description: The name a gate asks for (`design-review`).

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn. Giving a sign-off needs no reason; taking one back does.

status.description: The status the item was in when it was given.

verdict.description:
`given`, or `withdrawn` (FEAT-182). A withdrawal is its own entry, appended like any other,
with an empty `rev`: an older kanbanr, which does not know this field, then reads the
latest entry as lapsed and stops counting the sign-off too.

SignoffVerdict.description: Whether a sign-off entry gives the sign-off or takes it back (FEAT-182).

Source.description:
Where an imported feature came from (FEAT-042). This is a record of history, not a live
pointer: the original text is preserved in the feature's spec, so nothing depends on the
source still existing (a deleted file, rewritten git history, a removed issue).

imported_at.description: When it was imported (RFC 3339); stamped by kanbanr.

key.description: Stable identity used to skip re-imports; derived by kanbanr when not given.

missing_since.description: When the source was found to be gone (set by `kanbanr sources --write`).

ref.description: Location in that tracker, for humans: `TODO.md:14`, `owner/repo#123`, `PROJ-45`.

revision.description: Project repo commit at import time (file sources).

capacity.description: What the sprint can take, in the project's estimate unit.

carried.description: What left unfinished, and where it went — the record a retro reads.

goal.description: What this sprint is for, in a sentence.

SprintCarry.description: An item that left a sprint unfinished, and where it went.

to.description: The sprint it moved to, or `backlog`.

SprintReport.description: A sprint as a report: its record, what it holds, and how it burned down.

capacity.description: What the sprint can take, in the project's estimate unit.

carried.description: What left unfinished, and where it went — the record a retro reads.

days_left.description: Days left, counting today; 0 once the sprint is over.

goal.description: What this sprint is for, in a sentence.

unestimated.description: Items with no estimate in the project's unit: they count as nothing, which is said, not hidden.

SprintState.description: Where a sprint is in its life.

StageChange.description:
One move of a release between stages: where to, who moved it, and when (FEAT-183). A move back
carries the reason it was made.

interest.description: What they need from this project, and why they care.

Task.description: A todo item belonging to a todo-list. `key` is short and unique within its todo-list.

TaskState.description: Tri-state for a feature's todo items.

TestRef.description: A test that verifies a requirement, and where it currently stands.

checked_rev.description:
The project revision at which this was last observed green. A green older than HEAD is
stale rather than trustworthy.

kind.description: unit | integration | e2e | manual | property — free text, like `kind` elsewhere.

name.description: The test's name as it appears in the codebase, so it can be checked for existence.

TestState.description:
The TDD lifecycle of a test: written but not yet run, failing, passing.

Serialized lowercase (`state: green`) because that is how it is written in definition files and
on the command line; the aliases keep hand-written YAML forgiving.

TodoList.description:
A persistent todo-list attached to a feature item. A feature (acting as an epic) can hold
many of these — e.g. one added per working session — so the work survives across sessions.

cost.description: The quality spent for it. A decision with no cost is usually one nobody examined.

Transition.description: One status change. Append-only: the board's memory of how work actually moved.

override.description: Why a gate was passed over, when it was (FEAT-113). Absent on an ordinary move.

Zachman.description: The six completeness dimensions. Answers are one line; anything longer belongs in the spec.

info.description: The read-only routes `kanbanr serve` answers for the monitor and for tools built on the board. Version 1 stays at `/api/...`; a breaking change would be published as v2 under `/api/v2/...`, with v1 kept for a deprecation period. Routes the daemon serves that are not listed here are internal and may change. Write routes (`serve --allow-writes`) are not part of this contract. Errors are `text/plain`. CORS is permissive; there is no authentication.
